meta.title: ADA education
meta.description: The ADA curriculum: the Postpartum Doula Program and its {count} modules, continuing education, and how to teach the ADA curriculum as a trainer or training provider.

hero.title: Learn the ADA curriculum.
hero.line: ADA writes the curriculum. ADA Certified Trainers and Approved Training Providers teach it, and ADA examines every candidate.
hero.photoAlt: An instructor of the ADA Postpartum Doula Program teaches beside a slide, with training dolls and baby baths on the table

tiles.title: ADA programs
tiles.postpartumText: ADA’s core curriculum: {count} modules, in person over {days} days or online, then the ADA exam. Tuition is set by the training provider.
tiles.birthText: Labor and delivery support. Cohorts run on a rolling basis.
tiles.coursesText: IBCLC Exam-Prep, Continuing Education and Train-the-Trainer, taught by ADA Certified Trainers.

how.title: How ADA education works
how.photoAlt: A trainee dresses a training doll during a newborn-care lesson of the ADA Postpartum Doula Program
how.photoCaption: A newborn-care lesson with a training doll. August 2024.
how.curriculumText: ADA writes and owns the curriculum and the standards behind every ADA program. Every trainer and every provider teaches the same material.
how.teachingText: ADA Certified Trainers and Approved Training Providers teach it, in person and online. ADA reviews every provider each year.
how.examinationText: ADA examines and grades every candidate itself. Trainers, proctors and providers cannot change scores.
how.registryText: Graduates who pass get a certificate number and a public, dated record in the ADA registry. ADA Certified Trainers have public records too.

program.title: The Postpartum Doula Program
program.intro: ADA’s core curriculum, taught by an ADA Certified Trainer or an Approved Training Provider. Before class, each student works through short skills videos with exercises.
program.formatValue: In person, {days} days of intensive instruction, or online.
program.tuitionValue: Set by the trainer or training provider
program.leadsToValue: The ADA Postpartum Doula exam. The exam fee is {fee}, paid to ADA.
program.ctaNext: Graduates can register for the {date} exam.
program.ctaNone: Graduates register for the ADA exam with ADA.

module.postpartumRecovery: Stages of body recovery, wound care assessment, vital-sign monitoring, and traditional recovery principles such as warming and circulation.
module.newbornCare: Bottle and breast feeding technique, bathing and umbilical care, safe sleep, soothing, burping, diapering, spit-up, tummy time and milestone tracking.
module.breastfeedingSupport: Latch and positioning, engorgement, low supply and nipple pain, pumping, and when to refer to a lactation consultant.
module.culturalTraditions: Chinese zuo yuezi (<zh>坐月子</zh>), Korean sanhujori (<ko>산후조리</ko>) and Japanese satogaeri (<ja>里帰り</ja>), along with confinement meals and family dynamics.
module.nutrition: Postpartum recipes across Asian traditions, and dietary guidance for breastfeeding.
module.emotionalWellness: Recognizing perinatal depression and anxiety, active listening, stigma, boundaries and referral protocols.
module.safetyEmergency: Infant CPR ({provider}), choking response, emergency protocols, safe-sleep setup, and when to call {emergency} and when to call the pediatrician.

dates.title: Upcoming ADA exam dates
dates.intro: Each trainer or training provider sets its own session dates and handles enrollment and tuition. When you finish the program, you register for the ADA exam with ADA. The exam fee is {fee}.

teach.title: Continuing education and teaching
teach.ceText: ADA-approved workshops and updated coursework that keep certified doulas current with postpartum care and safety protocols.
teach.trainerText: For experienced ADA-certified doulas in good standing who want to teach the ADA curriculum, through Train-the-Trainer. An ADA Certified Trainer has a TR certificate number.
teach.providerText: For organizations that deliver the ADA curriculum. ADA reviews each provider every year against its standards for facilities, curriculum delivery and instructor qualifications.
teach.apply: To apply as a trainer or a provider, write to ADA at <mail>{email}</mail>.
teach.verifyText: Every ADA Certified Trainer holds an ADA certificate with a public, dated record in the ADA registry. Look it up by name or certificate number.
